headline: U.S. 30-Year Mortgage Rate Eases to 7.32% in First Decline Since August
summary: The average long-term U.S. mortgage rate fell to 7.32% last week, marking its first pullback since late August and offering slight relief to prospective homebuyers facing high borrowing costs.
why: Mortgage rate fluctuations directly influence housing market affordability, home sales volume, and mortgage origination revenues for financial institutions.

impacts.name: Real Estate
impacts.why: Lower mortgage rates reduce borrowing costs, potentially stimulating homebuyer demand.

why_moved: A pullback in benchmark borrowing costs eases pressures on prospective homebuyers, supporting sentiment in interest-sensitive real estate sectors.
